ncaaf_intelligence.engineering_constraints: The source surface itself implies a batch/data-engineering problem: 130+ FBS teams plus FCS/lower divisions require classification-aware IDs, historical/conference-season joins, neutralSite/location handling, and a single canonical schedule. A 60-game Saturday should be handled by season/week prefetch, server-side caching, idempotent upserts and queued line snapshots—not per-user live fan-out. cfbfastR documents season-vector loaders and direct database writes; CFBD documents classifications, neutralSite and paid quotas. These are engineering recommendations, not a claim that any competitor has solved them.

accuracy_distribution_70_percent_problem.defensible_claim_threshold: No universal numeric “maximum” can be derived from these sources. The defensible ceiling is a narrowly scoped, pre-registered and reproducible claim: report sport/market, line timestamp (open/close), N, selection rule, units/ROI, CLV, confidence intervals and all picks—including losses—on a held-out time period. GSE should not advertise “70% ATS long-term” or imply SU equals betting profit; a safer claim is a transparent historical result such as “X% ATS on N specified bets versus the closing line,” with the audit link and limitations. This is an evidentiary/marketing recommendation, not legal advice.
accuracy_distribution_70_percent_problem.regulatory_risks: FTC guidance says advertising claims must be truthful, non-deceptive/unfair and evidence-based. The fetched New York AG alert documents misleading “risk-free” and $1,000 offer claims with play-through conditions; Connecticut DCP announced a DraftKings settlement requiring more than $3m returned to 7,000 consumers, $50,000 and marketing-law training; a legal report says NY false-advertising settlements with DraftKings/FanDuel totaled $12m and required disclosures including user success rates/top-winner concentration. FTC-specific action against a sports-picks/tipster service was NOT FETCHED in this run. Avoid guaranteed wins, risk-free wording without prominent conditions, cherry-picked streaks, and unsupported typical-user earnings/profit claims.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Guo et al. describe temperature scaling as a one-parameter post-processing method and report it effective on most tested neural-network datasets.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: High baseline value when logits are miscalibrated; low parameter variance and easy monitoring. It cannot fix class/region-specific distortion—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Low: fit one temperature only inside each rolling training fold; retain separate sport/market checks.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Platt is a smooth low-parameter map; isotonic is flexible monotone nonparametric calibration. Thin samples favor Platt/temperature; isotonic needs enough out-of-sample points and can overfit—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Improves probability reliability when distortion is smooth; isotonic can capture non-sigmoid shape when data support it. Validate by rolling log loss/Brier, not in-sample fit.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Low–medium: both are standard; isotonic requires guardrails/minimum-bin rules and more monitoring.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Beta calibration is a richer class of maps based on the beta distribution; authors report superiority to logistic calibration for Naive Bayes and AdaBoost in their experiments.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Candidate gain for asymmetric tails and non-logistic distortions; transfer to NCAAF/DFS is unverified and must be measured out of sample—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Medium: implement and constrain parameters, fit only within time folds and monitor tail stability.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Roelofs et al. find equal-mass bins lower bias than equal-width bins and propose a debiased estimator/ECE_sweep; scikit-learn documents reliability diagrams and warns scalar Brier alone is not calibration.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: High measurement gain on thin slices: less binning bias and honest bootstrap uncertainty; this improves selection of calibrator rather than accuracy by itself—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Low–medium: add equal-mass/debiased estimators, bootstrap intervals and reliability plots to the evaluation pipeline.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Brier score should be decomposed into reliability, resolution and uncertainty; lower Brier alone does not guarantee better calibration.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: High diagnostic value: separates probability calibration from discrimination and base-rate randomness; no guaranteed ROI uplift.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Low: compute decomposition alongside log loss, ATS and CLV by sport/season.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Hierarchical models estimate global performance plus group effects and shrink low-information groups toward the global mean, accounting for unequal sample sizes.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Meaningful variance reduction for thin NCAAF sport/league/market slices; exact gain is unverified and should be measured by rolling held-out calibration—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Medium–high: Bayesian fitting, prior design, drift monitoring and serving posterior uncertainty.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: TimeSeriesSplit trains on earlier folds and tests on the next; its gap excludes samples immediately before a test set. All calibration, feature transforms, ownership data and tuning must be nested historically.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Highest expected reliability/credibility gain because it prevents future information contaminating the result; effect size not verified.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Medium: event-time data contracts, rolling feature stores, nested folds and immutable line snapshots.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Conformal methods provide model-agnostic intervals with coverage guarantees under relevant assumptions; the time-series tutorial uses cross-validation-calibrated intervals.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Adds uncertainty bands/sets for player outcomes and NCAAF predictions; coverage is conditional on stability/exchangeability, so monitor drift—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Medium: rolling residual stores, sport-specific coverage monitoring and interval-aware UX.

methodology_and_calibration.citation: Optimizer prior art uses salary/roster/scoring constraints, locks/exclusions, expert projections, projected ownership, floor/ceiling sorting and stacking rules.
methodology_and_calibration.expected_gain: Potential leverage/diversification gain, not verified ROI; treat ownership as uncertain and backtest contest-specific utility—engineering judgment.
methodology_and_calibration.implementation_cost: Medium: ingest ownership forecasts, solve constrained portfolios, and calibrate against contest payout/rake.
